evals.prompt: I am buried in email after PTO—triage my inbox, propose three concrete next actions, and draft replies where appropriate. Do not send any email; leave everything as drafts or a checklist for my approval.
evals.expected_output: Prioritized triage with at most three highlighted actions; any mail work is explicitly draft-only; user approval is required before send.
expectations: The response states or implies that outbound email will not be sent without explicit user approval
The response proposes at most three distinct prioritized actions or threads (not an unfocused dump)
The response references triage, inbox, or backlog context appropriate to post-PTO catch-up

evals.prompt:
Here is a short fictional meeting transcript for testing only:

Alice: We will send the revised contract by Friday.
Bob: Please add a Planner task for me to review the SLA.
Alice: I will email the customer the kickoff deck tonight.

Extract action items with owners, suggest tasks for the task system, and draft any promised outbound email as drafts only. Do not send.
evals.expected_output: Structured action items; tasks identified; promised customer email handled as draft; no send.
expectations: The response lists action items or tasks with at least one clear owner or assignee where stated in the transcript
The response does not claim that an email was sent to the customer
The response treats the customer email or kickoff deck commitment as something to draft or queue for approval rather than as already delivered

evals.prompt: Produce a weekday morning briefing for me in under 250 words. Assume I have two meetings today (10:00 standup, 14:00 vendor call) and three overdue tasks (expenses, slide deck, HR form). Use the personal-assistant morning briefing style: meetings with brief context, max three inbox-priority lines, and a short proactive section. Do not invent real email content—use placeholders if needed.
evals.expected_output: Scannable briefing under ~250 words with sections for today, inbox priority (≤3), and proactive note; no fabricated private details.
expectations: The response is clearly under roughly 250 words (briefing discipline)
The response mentions both meetings or their times in a Today-style section
The response limits explicit inbox or task callouts to three or fewer items or clearly groups extras as secondary
